predecessors.name: Salian Franks
predecessors.text: the Salian realm of Tournai with Clovis's Soissons and the northern Alemanni (the 500 shape), the core of the 510 shape

predecessors.name: Ripuarian Franks
predecessors.text: the Ripuarian kingdom around Cologne, absorbed c.

predecessors.name: Visigothic Kingdom
predecessors.text: most of Aquitaine, taken at Vouillé in 507 ('The battle added most of Aquitaine to Clovis's kingdom', Clovis I page)

successors.name: West Francia
successors.text: 'all lands west of the Rhône, called West Francia' (Treaty of Verdun page), Charles the Bald

successors.name: Middle Francia
successors.text: 'the Low Countries, the Rhineland west of the Rhine, Lorraine, Alsace, Burgundy, Provence' and the kingdom of Italy, with Aachen and Rome: Lothair I

successors.name: East Francia
successors.text: 'all lands to the east of the Rhine', Louis the German

rulers.name: Pepin of Herstal
rulers.title: mayor of the palace of Austrasia, Neustria and Burgundy; Duke and Prince of the Franks

rulers.name: Pepin the Short
rulers.title: mayor of the palace of Neustria; King of the Franks from 751

rulers.name: Charlemagne
rulers.title: King of the Franks; King of the Lombards from 774; Emperor from 25 December 800

rulers.name: Louis the Pious
rulers.title: King of the Franks and Emperor

ledger.x: 509: Clovis I unites all the Franks.
509: the Ripuarian Franks are absorbed.
27 November 511: Clovis dies and his four sons divide the kingdom.
532: Thuringia joins the Franks.
532: the Franks take Autun, opening the last Burgundian war.
534: the Burgundian kingdom ends.
534: Burgundy becomes Frankish.
534: 29 Alpine cells held by the Ostrogoths in 533 enter Cliopatria's Frankish shape with Burgundy.
536: the Ostrogoths cede Provence.
555: Chlothar I makes the Saxons tributary.
556: the Saxons throw off the tribute.
561: Chlothar I dies and Guntram takes Burgundy.
561: 34 cells (Alpine and Mediterranean edge) pass to Cliopatria's Eastern Roman row; the pages opened are silent.
567: Cliopatria draws Thuringia as its own duchy.
599: Dormelles.
602: the Basques submit.
612: Theudebert II is crushed.
613: Chlothar II reunites the Franks.
629: Chlothar II dies and Charibert II takes Aquitaine.
632: Aquitaine returns.
633: Cliopatria folds Thuringia into the Frankish shape for 633-640 and its Duchy of Thuringia row has no shape; read as the end of the dependent duchy.
633: Thuringia is inside the Frankish shape again; page silent, see the vassal_end above.
639: Dagobert I dies; Clovis II takes Neustria and Burgundy.
641: Radulf breaks away in Thuringia.
644: 241 Swabian cells leave the Frankish shape.
661: Neustria and Burgundy return to this state.
690-692: Utrecht falls.
21 March 717: Charles Martel defeats the Neustrians at Vinchy.
718: Cliopatria hands 31 West Frisian cells (Utrecht) back to its Magna Frisia row; Radbod's Frisia is Frisian until his death in 719.
718: Cliopatria's Frankish shape takes 240 Swabian cells (7.3-11.1 E, 46.9-50.5 N) from its 'Frisia Kingdom' row, whose outline is Alamannia, not Frisia.
719: Charles Martel takes West Frisia.
724: Neustria is back inside the Frankish realm.
724: Alamannia stands apart.
724: Thuringia joins the Frankish shape as Cliopatria's Duchy of Thuringia row ends in 723.
730: Charles marches on Alamannia.
731: Charles Martel attacks Aquitaine.
732: the Umayyad army is beaten 'at the Battle of Tours at a location between Tours and Poitiers'.
732: Alamannia passes to the Franks in Cliopatria; the page dates only the 730 campaign.
732: Alamannia is in the Frankish shape.
734: the Frisians beaten on the Boarn.
738: Charles Martel makes the Saxons of Westphalia tributary.
739: Charles Martel secures Provence and Septimania.
751: Pepin the Short is elected king; the Carolingians replace the Merovingians.
755: 44 cells of Septimania (2.5-4.4 E, 43.4-47.4 N) enter Cliopatria's Frankish shape.
759: Pepin takes Narbonne.
760: Pepin opens the war on Waiofar's Aquitaine: 'In 760, after conquering the Roussillon from the defeated Muslims and denouncing Waiofar's actions,...'
768: Waiofar is assassinated.
768: Aquitaine falls to the Franks.

772: the Saxon tribute of 738 lapses in the Frankish invasion; the Saxon Wars page opens with 'the subjugation of the Engrians and destruction of their sacred symbol Irminsul near Paderborn in 772 or 773 at Eresburg'.
772: Charlemagne invades Saxony.
772: Cliopatria's Magna Frisia row ends in 771 and its 33 cells join the Frankish shape; the Charles Martel page dates the Frankish victory in Frisia to 734.
773: Charlemagne besieges Pavia.
774: Pavia surrenders.
774: Charlemagne is King of the Lombards.
775: Saxony conquered but for Nordalbingia.
775: Saxony passes to the Franks.
775: 56 cells of Romagna (11.2-13.4 E, 43.4-45.1 N) held by the Papal States row in 774 are inside Cliopatria's Frankish shape.
778: Cliopatria takes Saxony out of the Frankish shape.
778: 73 cells of the Duchy of Spoleto (12.2-13.9 E, 41.9-43.5 N) enter the Frankish shape as Cliopatria's Spoleto row ends in 777.
778: 53 cells of the Ebro valley (-2.1 to 1.6 E, 41.5-42.7 N) enter the Frankish shape; they leave again in 783.
779: Charlemagne reconquers Saxony.
781: Louis is made king of Aquitaine.
782: Widukind's revolt.
782: the rebels hold Saxony (Westphalia, Engria, Eastphalia).
783: 49 Frisian cells (5.4-8.3 E, 52.8-53.6 N) leave Cliopatria's Frankish shape for its Frisia row (783-787).
783: the 53 Ebro cells of 778 leave the Frankish shape again.

783: 129 cells of Gascony (-1.5 to 1.2 E, 42.8-44.7 N) enter the Frankish shape from Cliopatria's Duchy of Gascony row; the Louis the Pious page has Pepin's kingdom of Aquitaine in 817 'including Gascony'.
785: Widukind is baptised.
785: Saxony is Frankish again; 'the land had peace for the next seven years, though revolts continued sporadically until 804'.
786: Benevento submits.
787: Charlemagne invades Bavaria.
788: Tassilo III is deposed.
788: Bavaria becomes Frankish.
788: 49 Frisian cells return (5.4-8.3 E) as Cliopatria's Frisia row (783-787) ends.
Summer 791: Charlemagne invades the Avar khaganate.
October 791: the campaign ends.
793: the Saxons rise again.
793: the revolt spreads from Westphalia to Eastphalia and Nordalbingia.
793: Cliopatria's Benevento row returns (793-849) and the 152 cells leave the Frankish shape.
793: 33 Frisian cells leave for Cliopatria's Frisians row (793-799).
794: the revolt is over, 'completely put down by 794'.
794: Saxony is Frankish again; 'An Engrian rebellion followed closely in 796, but Charlemagne's personal presence... immediately crushed it'.
796: Pippin of Italy takes Pannonia.
800: 33 Frisian cells return from Cliopatria's Frisians row (ends 799).
800: 121 Avar cells (the Danube-Tisza land) leave the Frankish shape.
800: the court settles at Aachen.
25 December 800: Charlemagne is crowned emperor.
801: Barcelona falls.
804: Nordalbingia goes to the Obotrites.
806: 79 cells of the Croatian coast (14.4-16.8 E, 43.7-45.4 N) enter the shape as Cliopatria's Duchy of Croatia row (741-925) is cut there.
814: 38 cells on the eastern edge (8.8-18.9 E, 46.0-54.5 N) go to Cliopatria's Great Moravia row (3 more to Nitra): the Slavic marches.
814: 13 northern cells go to Cliopatria's Scandinavian row; the Charlemagne page has the Danish king Gudfred murdered in 810 and a settlement in 811 ('Hemming later sued for peace').
825: 24 cells of Pamplona (and 15 of Sobrarbe) leave the Frankish shape.
827: the Bulgars take the March of Pannonia.
840: 125 Pannonian cells come back from Cliopatria's Bulgarian row; no page opened shows a Frankish reconquest.
August 843: Aquitaine passes with West Francia.
10 August 843: Charles the Bald receives West Francia.
10 August 843: Lothair I receives Middle Francia.
10 August 843: Louis the German receives East Francia.
10 August 843: the Treaty of Verdun ends the one Frankish realm.

wars.name: Frankish conquest of Burgundy
wars.outcome: The Franks lost at Vézeronce on 25 June 524 (Chlodomer killed), took Autun in 532 and ended the Burgundian kingdom in 534; it was divided among the three Frankish rulers.

wars.name: Frankish conquest of Thuringia
wars.outcome: Thuringia was conquered by Theuderic and Chlothar with Theudebert I's help and incorporated in 532.

wars.name: Saxon revolt of 555-556
wars.outcome: Chlothar I imposed an annual tribute in 555; the Saxons revolted again between 555 and 556; no border moved.

wars.name: Wars of Chlothar II against his nephews
wars.outcome: Dormelles 599: Chlothar II was reduced to Beauvais, Amiens and Rouen; a first attempt at reconquest failed in 604; Theudebert was crushed at Toul and Tolbiac in 612; the whole realm was delivered to Chlothar in 613.

wars.name: Wendish war of Dagobert I
wars.outcome: Dagobert's Austrasian forces lost at Wogastisburg in 631; his Alemannic and Lombard allies repelled the Wends, who attacked again the next year; the Saxons offered help in return for ending their tribute of 500 cows.

wars.name: Revolt of Radulf in Thuringia
wars.outcome: Thuringia leaves direct Frankish rule under Radulf.

wars.name: Neustrian-Austrasian wars and the Battle of Tertry
wars.outcome: Ebroin nearly united all the Franks and was assassinated in 681; at Tertry in 687 Pepin of Herstal defeated the king and his mayor and became mayor of Austrasia, Neustria and Burgundy.

wars.name: Frisian wars of Pepin of Herstal and Charles Martel
wars.outcome: Utrecht fell between 690 and 692; Charles seized West Frisia on Radbod's death in 719; he beat the Frisians on the Boarn in 734.

wars.name: Civil war after Pepin of Herstal
wars.outcome: Compiègne 26 September 715, Vinchy 21 March 717, Soissons 718 (Chilperic II and Odo of Aquitaine defeated); Charles Martel acclaimed mayor over Austrasia in 718; Chilperic II died in 721 and Charles appointed Theuderic IV.

wars.name: Charles Martel's campaigns in Bavaria and Alamannia
wars.outcome: Fighting in Bavaria 720-723, again in 725 and 728 (Duke Hugbert 'submitted to Frankish suzerainty'); in 730 Charles marched against Lantfrid, Duke of Alemannia, who had also become independent.

wars.name: Charles Martel's war with Aquitaine and the Umayyad invasion
wars.outcome: Charles attacked Aquitaine in 731; the Umayyad army was defeated at the Battle of Tours between Tours and Poitiers in 732.

wars.name: Charles Martel's campaigns in Provence and Septimania
wars.outcome: Campaigning in Provence and Septimania in 737; the uprising of Maurontus in Provence was checked in 739; Charles reorganised Burgundy 732-735.

wars.name: Conquest of Septimania
wars.outcome: Pepin chased the Arabs and Berbers from Septimania and conquered Narbonne in 759.

wars.name: War of Aquitaine
wars.outcome: Pepin opened the war in 760, captured strongholds in 763, Toulouse and Bordeaux in 767; Waiofar was assassinated in 768 and Hunald's capture under Charlemagne ended 'ten years of war'.

wars.name: Lombard campaign of Charlemagne
wars.outcome: Pavia besieged in late 773; Desiderius deposed and Charlemagne King of the Lombards in 774.

wars.name: Saxon Wars
wars.outcome: Eresburg 772; Saxony but for Nordalbingia taken 775; reconquest 779; Widukind's revolt 782-785 (Süntel, Verden, baptism 785); revolt 792-794; Engrian rising 796; Bornhöved 798; 10,000 deported and their land given to the Obotrites 804.

wars.name: Basque and Spanish campaigns
wars.outcome: The Roncevaux ambush of 778; Barcelona fell in 797, was retaken in 799 and conquered in 801 after a seven-month siege.

wars.name: Deposition of Tassilo III of Bavaria
wars.outcome: 787 invasion; Tassilo deposed and sent to a monastery in 788; Bavaria absorbed.

wars.name: Avar Wars
wars.outcome: 791 invasion beaten back by a horse epidemic; 793 abandoned for the Saxon revolt; 796 Pippin of Italy's army destroyed the khagan's 'ring' and the khagan submitted: 'Pannonia seized by Francia'.

wars.name: Danish war of Charlemagne
wars.outcome: Charlemagne sent an army to secure Frisia against Gudfred (810); Gudfred was murdered; a settlement with Hemming followed in 811.

wars.name: Breton campaign of Louis the Pious
wars.outcome: Louis was returning from a campaign to Brittany in 818 when he heard of Ermengarde's death.

wars.name: Frankish-Bulgarian war in Pannonia
wars.outcome: The Bulgarians attacked the Franks in the March of Pannonia and regained their lands.

wars.name: Revolts against Louis the Pious
wars.outcome: Pepin of Aquitaine marched on Paris and Louis was captured near Compiègne (830); Field of Lies 833; Louis restored on 1 March 834.

wars.name: Carolingian civil war
wars.outcome: Lothair I claimed overlordship after Louis's death in 840; Louis the German and Charles the Bald beat him at Fontenoy in 841 and swore the Oaths of Strasbourg in 842; the Treaty of Verdun was agreed on 10 August 843.

certainty.note: Merovingian frontiers are approximate: the shapes are Cliopatria's and the pages give cities and peoples, not lines.
Carolingian marches (Spanish, Breton, Pannonian, Saxon, Danish) were frontier zones; the Pyrenean and Elbe frontiers are the firmest, the Avar and Slavic ones the softest.

Treaty of Verdun: 'all lands west of the Rhône' and 'all lands to the east of the Rhine' are river lines; the page gives no line for Middle Francia's western edge (Scheldt, Meuse, Saône are not named).
